comment: The machine v0.1 conformance floor. Accepts carry structural expectations (identity, counts, service start order, granted capability set, and where it matters the folded rationale); rejects carry the fragment the refusal must contain, so a runtime refusing for the wrong reason fails (exemplar gap G8, applied from birth). Three of the accepts are the three profiles a machine can declare: a hosted box, an edge sensor, a touch phone. v0.1 widened 2026-09-12 (OS-4) with the BOARD clause: A9, R33, R34, R35 are the board's own; A1 and A2 carry the defaulted and the declared board. Widened again 2026-09-12 (the NETWORK kind): A10, A11, R36-R40; A2 is the box file with its NETWORK; every accept's counts carry networks. Widened again 2026-09-12 (SLOTS, A/B): A12, R41, R42. Widened again 2026-09-12 (READY, a daemon's own signal): A13, R43, R44, R45. Widened again 2026-09-12 (USER, a declared identity): A14, R46-R50; every accept's counts carry users. Widened again 2026-09-12 (the edge boards): A3 becomes machines/cold_room_sensor.machine verbatim with BOARD pico2; A15, R51, R52; R35 now refuses a hosted board on an edge machine by profile. Widened again 2026-10-04 (FORWARD, the way between networks): A27-A29, R95-R103; a machine says it forwards, never assumes it, one network (and a loopback is not one) has nothing to forward between, a machine that forwards cannot say there is no way off a link it joins, and one machine answers for a domain once. Widened again 2026-10-05 (STATE, a world's own directory): A30-A35, R104-R138; a world that runs as an identity owns the directories it names and nothing else of the machine's, only an identity can own one, only where the machine can hand one over (under /run, or inside an ext4 or tmpfs mount the world keeps and that is not read-only, with every mount above it kept too), no two worlds own overlapping directories, a world's signal sits directly in its own directory and never in a neighbour's, the floor's own key and record are in no directory a world owns, and the paths the court compares are plain names of bounded length, so that no spelling reaches one file by two names. Two rules about mounts came with it, because a directory's holder is the innermost mount only if the outer one is declared first and no two share a mount point. Widened again 2026-10-05 (the time seat, TIME-1): A36-A43, R139-R170; time enters a record only as an authority's signed statement, so a machine declares the clock it HAS (a plain device path under /dev, and a key to sign with), a link it answers the time on (one, a static address, a port from 1024 to 65535, never a loopback, never asking anybody), or whom it asks and whose word it takes (a journal to date, an address and a port from 1 to 65535 each spelled one way, a way there, and one spelling of a key that is a key); and a clock is a real-time clock, not any device. The boundary cases are here because a probe with a mutated court found the first version of these fixtures judged none of them: A38-A40 and R159-R162 are what that probe asked for; A41-A43 and R164-R170 are what an independent review of the seat asked for. Widened again 2026-10-13 (the reservation, TIM-1): A44-A51, R171-R194; a world may ask the kernel for time it will get every period -- a PERIOD, a DEADLINE and a RUNTIME in microseconds and the CORE it runs on, the four together -- and a hosted machine says how many CORES it has (2 to 64; a Raspberry Pi 4 has four); the runtime fits the deadline and the deadline the period, a runtime of ten microseconds at least and a period within the kernel's own bounds (100 us to 4194304 us), core 0 is the machine's, the reservations on one core sum to no more than the 90 per cent the kernel gives (it admits 95 and holds 5 for the ordinary tasks' own deadline server), counted as the kernel counts it, and a world with a reservation declares no CPU ceiling. The kernel judges the same set again at the act, and refuses what does not fit. Widened again 2026-10-14 (the ports a world may bind, PORT-1): A52-A53, R195-R206; a world that runs as an identity and speaks on the network may be given the TCP ports it will bind -- one to eight of them, 1 to 65535, a list of numbers and nothing else -- and no other: the kernel holds it to them with a rule set, and gives a port below 1024 only to a world that declares it; only an identity can be given a port, a world kept off the network has nothing to bind, and one port is bound by one world. Widened again 2026-10-19 (the mirror, MIR-1): A54-A59, R210-R249; a machine gives the copy of a world's directory or takes one, never both, and says which with a key it is told: the source declares the directory (inside a world's STATE, on a disk that keeps owners), the one device it is given to and the link it is given on (a TCP port from 1024 to 65535, a static address, never a loopback, one link); the destination declares whom it takes from, whose word it takes, where it keeps the copy (on a disk that keeps modes, writable, not the root of the disk, not in a world's place, and not where any name the floor makes for the copy would land on the key or the record) and how often it asks (5 seconds to a day). Both ends sign, so both need an IDENTITY, and an address and a key are each one spelling of a key that is one.

accepts.name: the minimal machine: one MACHINE declaration, defaults stated

DEFINE MACHINE hello AS (
  PROFILE hosted,
  ARCH x86_64,

) RATIONALE "The smallest declarable machine"

accepts.name: the hosted box: the counter machine of a restaurant, whole -- machines/makeen_box.machine verbatim
accepts.source:
-- makeen_box.machine -- the box behind the counter: server, network and
-- bridge in one. The hosted profile's reference machine (fixture A2 is
-- this file, verbatim) and, since OS-4, the board's truth: a Raspberry
-- Pi 4 Model B, the SD card's second partition as /data, the console on
-- the header pins, the network declared and brought up by PID 1 before
-- any world speaks, and two boot slots: an update is tried once under
-- the watchdog and committed only when every world is SERVING -- and
-- still serving a window later -- and the box recognises its own boot. RestoLean's Makeen thread named the box;
-- this declares it.

DEFINE MACHINE makeen_box AS (
  PROFILE hosted,
  ARCH aarch64,
  KERNEL linux,
  LIBC musl,
  BOARD rpi4,
  CONSOLE "/dev/ttyS1",
  SLOTS "/dev/mmcblk0p1",
  IDENTITY "/data/device.key",
  JOURNAL "/data/boot.journal"
) RATIONALE "One box, no shell, no package manager: the declared machine is the system; two slots, so an update is a trial before it is a commitment"

DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (
  GRANT yes
) RATIONALE "The box is the restaurant's network"

DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (
  GRANT yes
) RATIONALE "Orders and stock live on the box"

DEFINE CAPABILITY gpio AS (
  GRANT no
) RATIONALE "No pins on the counter box; sensors are edge machines"

DEFINE MOUNT data AS (
  AT "/data",
  FS ext4,
  DEVICE "/dev/mmcblk0p2",
  OPTIONS [rw, noatime]
) RATIONALE "The persistent partition: the SD card's second partition"

DEFINE NETWORK lan AS (
  INTERFACE "eth0",
  ADDRESS "192.168.10.1/24"
) RATIONALE "The box is the network's address; the phones find it here. No gateway: the box is the gateway"

DEFINE SERVICE kds AS (
  RUN ["/stzr", "/app/kds.luau"],
  RESTART always,
  READY "/run/kds.ready",
  HEALTH 5,
  NEEDS [network, filesystem]
) RATIONALE "The kitchen display world: a daemon that serves the kitchen and says so by creating its READY path; PID 1 keeps it alive for the life of the box"

DEFINE SERVICE poste AS (
  RUN ["/stzr", "/app/poste.luau"],
  RESTART always,
  READY "/run/poste.ready",
  HEALTH 5,
  AFTER [kds],
  NEEDS [network, filesystem]
) RATIONALE "The counter world: a daemon too, and it starts only once the kitchen display has SIGNALLED it is serving -- not merely started"

accepts.name: the edge sensor: no kernel, no libc, pins and a flash log -- machines/cold_room_sensor.machine verbatim
accepts.source:
-- cold_room_sensor.machine -- the edge profile's reference machine, and
-- fixture A3 verbatim: the HACCP probe of RestoLean's cold room, the
-- sensor the Makeen box listens to. It is declared here and PROJECTED
-- onto MicroRing's substrate (`harb project`), never imaged and never
-- booted here: `harb init` refuses the edge profile by name and says
-- whose it is. MicroRing owns the firmware, the tiers and the loop.

DEFINE MACHINE cold_room_sensor AS (
  PROFILE edge,
  ARCH thumbv8m,
  KERNEL none,
  BOARD pico2
) RATIONALE "A thermistor, a log, a radio: the binary is the device"

DEFINE CAPABILITY gpio AS (
  GRANT yes
) RATIONALE "The probe and the LED are pins"

DEFINE CAPABILITY clock AS (
  GRANT yes
) RATIONALE "Readings are timestamped"

DEFINE PIN led AS (
  GPIO 25,
  MODE out
) RATIONALE "Heartbeat: the board's own LED, so a cold room says it is alive"

DEFINE PIN probe AS (
  GPIO 4,
  MODE in
) RATIONALE "The thermistor"

DEFINE MOUNT log AS (
  AT "/log",
  FS littlefs,
  DEVICE "flash0"
) RATIONALE "Power-loss safe, wear-levelled: a reading survives the power going out"

DEFINE SERVICE sense AS (
  RUN ["sense"],
  RESTART always,
  NEEDS [gpio, clock]
) RATIONALE "Read, log, sleep -- the behaviour itself is the Device language's, projected as a named seam"

accepts.name: AFTER orders the services; declaration order breaks ties
accepts.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "order"
DEFINE SERVICE c AS (RUN ["c"], AFTER [a, b]) RATIONALE "third"
DEFINE SERVICE b AS (RUN ["b"], AFTER [a]) RATIONALE "second"
DEFINE SERVICE a AS (RUN ["a"]) RATIONALE "first"

accepts.name: a declared identity, and a service that runs as it
accepts.source:

DEFINE USER kds AS (
  UID 1000,
  GID 1000
) RATIONALE "The kitchen display world owns nothing of the machine"
DEFINE USER poste AS (
  UID 1001
) RATIONALE "The counter world; its gid follows its uid unless declared"

  RUN ["/display"],
  USER kds,
  NEEDS [process]
) RATIONALE "Runs as the identity, not as the machine"

DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER u AS (UID 0) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: one number, one identity
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER a AS (UID 1000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER b AS (UID 1000) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: already a's; one number, one identity

rejects.name: USER is a hosted machine's declaration
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE edge, ARCH thumbv7em, KERNEL none) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER u AS (UID 1000) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a uid out of range is refused
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER u AS (UID 70000) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a hosted machine cannot name an edge board
rejects.source: DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH aarch64, KERNEL linux, BOARD pico2) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: a board of the edge profile

rejects.name: an edge board still owes its architecture
rejects.source: DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE edge, ARCH thumbv7em, KERNEL none, BOARD pico2) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: HEALTH is measured on the READY path: a service without one has nothing to refresh
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, HEALTH 5) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: HEALTH is measured on the READY path

rejects.name: a window of zero seconds is not a window
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, READY "/run/s.ready", HEALTH 0) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: HEALTH is a SERVICE's clause, not a MOUNT's
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS tmpfs, HEALTH 5) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a ceiling of zero mebibytes is not a ceiling
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART never, MEMORY 0) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a share of zero is a service that cannot run
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART never, CPU 0) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: CPU 0 is a service that cannot run

rejects.name: a share above sixteen cores is refused
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART never, CPU 2000) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: MEMORY is a SERVICE's clause, not a MACHINE's
rejects.source: DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, MEMORY 512) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a gateway is a way out: EGRESS none says there is none
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK lan AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "10.0.2.15/24", GATEWAY "10.0.2.2", EGRESS none) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: EGRESS none says there is none

rejects.name: an empty EGRESS is not a declaration
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK lan AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "10.0.2.15/24", EGRESS []) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a destination is an address and a prefix, never a host name
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK lan AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "10.0.2.15/24", EGRESS ["the ministry"]) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a machine that is granted no network cannot declare where it goes
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS tmpfs, EGRESS none) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a key lives at an absolute path, like everything else PID 1 must find
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, IDENTITY "device.key") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS ext4, DEVICE "/dev/vda") RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a key that dies with the power is a new device every morning
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, IDENTITY "/tmp/device.key") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT tmp AS (AT "/tmp", FS tmpfs) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: an edge device's identity is MicroRing's, and its custody is the hardware's
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE edge, ARCH thumbv8m, KERNEL none, BOARD pico2, IDENTITY "/log/device.key") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY gpio AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE PIN led AS (GPIO 25, MODE out) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: IDENTITY is a hosted machine's declaration

rejects.name: a journal is signed by the device, so the device needs a key
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, JOURNAL "/data/boot.journal") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS ext4, DEVICE "/dev/vda") RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a record that dies with the power is not a record
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, IDENTITY "/data/device.key", JOURNAL "/tmp/boot.journal") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS ext4, DEVICE "/dev/vda") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT tmp AS (AT "/tmp", FS tmpfs) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a journal lives at an absolute path, like the key that signs it
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, IDENTITY "/data/device.key", JOURNAL "boot.journal") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS ext4, DEVICE "/dev/vda") RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a peer of this link lives on this link

rejects.name: a name needs a domain to be a name

DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK lan AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.10.1/24") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE PEER imprimante AS (NETWORK lan, HARDWARE "b8:27:eb:11:22:33", ADDRESS "192.168.10.50") RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: one address, one peer

DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK lan AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.10.1/24", DOMAIN "makeen") RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a hardware address is six pairs, and the box hands out addresses by it
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK lan AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.10.1/24", DOMAIN "makeen") RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a peer belongs to a network this machine declared
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK lan AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.10.1/24", DOMAIN "makeen") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE PEER imprimante AS (NETWORK wifi, HARDWARE "b8:27:eb:11:22:33", ADDRESS "192.168.10.50") RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a peer's name has to be a name the wire can carry
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"

DEFINE NETWORK lan AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.10.1/24", DOMAIN "makeen") RATIONALE "x"

rejects.refusal: cannot be a name on makeen

rejects.name: a machine that asks for its own address is not the one that hands them out
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK lan AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS dhcp, DOMAIN "makeen") RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a world cannot choose sight of a filesystem it never asked for
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY process AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS tmpfs, OPTIONS [rw]) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT logs AS (AT "/var/log", FS tmpfs, OPTIONS [rw]) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE blind AS (
  RUN ["/w"],
  RESTART never,
  NEEDS [process],
  SEES [data]
) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a world sees a mount this machine declares, or none
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY process AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS tmpfs, OPTIONS [rw]) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT logs AS (AT "/var/log", FS tmpfs, OPTIONS [rw]) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE ledger AS (
  RUN ["/w"],
  RESTART never,
  NEEDS [process, filesystem],
  SEES [archives]
) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: an empty SEES is not a declaration
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY process AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS tmpfs, OPTIONS [rw]) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT logs AS (AT "/var/log", FS tmpfs, OPTIONS [rw]) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE ledger AS (
  RUN ["/w"],
  RESTART never,

) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: naming one mount twice says nothing the once did not
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY process AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS tmpfs, OPTIONS [rw]) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT logs AS (AT "/var/log", FS tmpfs, OPTIONS [rw]) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE ledger AS (
  RUN ["/w"],
  RESTART never,
  NEEDS [process, filesystem],
  SEES [data, data]
) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a machine that mounts nothing has no sight to apportion
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY process AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE ledger AS (
  RUN ["/w"],
  RESTART never,
  NEEDS [process, filesystem],
  SEES [data]
) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a world with no task at all cannot be a world
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY process AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE none AS (
  RUN ["/w"],
  RESTART never,
  NEEDS [process],
  TASKS 0
) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: the number counts tasks, and nothing else is being counted
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY process AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE vast AS (
  RUN ["/w"],
  RESTART never,
  NEEDS [process],
  TASKS 100000
) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a FLEET belongs to a fleet file: no machine says who else is in its estate
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE FLEET atelier AS () RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: FLEET belongs to a fleet file

rejects.name: a MEMBER belongs to a fleet file
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MEMBER caisse AS (DECLARATION "till.machine") RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: MEMBER belongs to a fleet file

rejects.name: a RETIREMENT belongs to a fleet file: which keys a device has held is a fact about a set
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE RETIREMENT carte_1 AS (MEMBER caisse, KEY "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa", THROUGH "8268cdcd77e480573bef62425e35af5cf938d837f3467c514fd2db198d43767a") RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: RETIREMENT belongs to a fleet file

rejects.name: everywhere has one spelling, and it is no EGRESS at all
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK lan AS (
  INTERFACE "eth0",
  ADDRESS "10.0.2.15/24",
  GATEWAY "10.0.2.2",
  EGRESS ["0.0.0.0/0"]
) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: the same claim in two pieces: EGR-2's lie, spelled so a prefix-0 check missed it
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK lan AS (
  INTERFACE "eth0",
  ADDRESS "10.0.2.15/24",
  GATEWAY "10.0.2.2",
  EGRESS ["0.0.0.0/1", "128.0.0.0/1"]
) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a prefix of 0 written over another address is still every address
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK lan AS (
  INTERFACE "eth0",
  ADDRESS "10.0.2.15/24",
  GATEWAY "10.0.2.2",
  EGRESS ["10.0.0.0/0"]
) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a console the board does not have: a PC's fifth serial port
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (
  PROFILE hosted,
  ARCH x86_64,
  KERNEL linux,
  CONSOLE "/dev/ttyS4"
) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: is not a console of BOARD qemu_pc

rejects.name: the Pi's PL011 is wired to its Bluetooth, not to the pins an operator listens on
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (
  PROFILE hosted,
  ARCH aarch64,
  KERNEL linux,
  BOARD rpi4,
  CONSOLE "/dev/ttyAMA0"
) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: is not a console of BOARD rpi4

rejects.name: a PC's serial port on the ARM emulator, which has one PL011
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (
  PROFILE hosted,
  ARCH aarch64,
  KERNEL linux,
  CONSOLE "/dev/ttyS0"
) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: is not a console of BOARD qemu_virt

rejects.name: the kernel's name for a port is not its device: CONSOLE names the device PID 1 speaks on
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (
  PROFILE hosted,
  ARCH x86_64,
  KERNEL linux,
  CONSOLE "ttyS0"
) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: is not a console of BOARD qemu_pc

rejects.name: forwarding between networks is a hosted machine's declaration: an edge machine is the way between nothing
rejects.source: DEFINE MACHINE s AS (PROFILE edge, ARCH thumbv7em, KERNEL none, FORWARD yes) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: FORWARD is a hosted machine's declaration

rejects.name: a machine that is not the way between networks declares nothing, never `FORWARD no`
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE gw AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, FORWARD no) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK front AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.20.1/24") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK core AS (INTERFACE "eth1", ADDRESS "10.20.0.1/24") RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: FORWARD takes a word, not a string
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE gw AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, FORWARD "yes") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK front AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.20.1/24") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK core AS (INTERFACE "eth1", ADDRESS "10.20.0.1/24") RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: one network has nothing to forward between
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE gw AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, FORWARD yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK front AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.20.1/24") RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: and it declares 1: a machine with fewer than two networks has nothing to forward between

rejects.name: no network at all has nothing to forward between either
rejects.source: DEFINE MACHINE gw AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, FORWARD yes) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: and it declares 0: a machine with fewer than two networks has nothing to forward between

rejects.name: a loopback is a network a machine declares and not a way to anywhere: one wire and a loopback is one link
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE gw AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, FORWARD yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK loopback AS (INTERFACE "lo", ADDRESS "127.0.0.1/8") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK front AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.20.1/24") RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: and it declares 1: a machine with fewer than two networks has nothing to forward between (a loopback is not a way to anywhere)

rejects.name: a machine that forwards is a way off every link it joins, so it cannot say EGRESS none for one of them
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE gw AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, FORWARD yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK front AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.20.1/24") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK core AS (INTERFACE "eth1", ADDRESS "10.20.0.1/24", EGRESS none) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: a machine that forwards is a way off every link it joins

rejects.name: a ROUTE belongs to a fleet file: which links are joined is a fact about a set, and no machine can say it
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE gw AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE ROUTE r AS (BETWEEN [front, core], THROUGH gw) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: ROUTE belongs to a fleet file, not a machine file

rejects.name: two networks of one machine answering to the same domain: a name on one link would be a name on both
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE gw AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK front AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.20.1/24", DOMAIN "cloud") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK core AS (INTERFACE "eth1", ADDRESS "10.20.0.1/24", DOMAIN "cloud") RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: core serves cloud, which front already serves

rejects.name: a directory is owned by an identity: a world with no USER is the machine itself, and a place made for it is made for nobody
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, STATE ["/run/s"]) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: an empty STATE says nothing: a world that keeps nothing of its own declares none
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, USER srv, STATE []) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: an empty STATE is not a declaration

rejects.name: STATE takes paths in strings, not words
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, USER srv, STATE [data]) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: STATE takes a list of paths in strings

rejects.name: a relative path is a place nobody can name
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, USER srv, STATE ["run/s"]) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: STATE is an absolute path of plain names

rejects.name: a path that climbs is a path to somewhere else: .. is refused wherever it stands
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, USER srv, STATE ["/run/../etc/s"]) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: STATE is an absolute path of plain names

rejects.name: a trailing slash names the same directory twice over
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, USER srv, STATE ["/run/s/"]) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: STATE is an absolute path of plain names

rejects.name: an empty name between slashes is not a name
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, USER srv, STATE ["/run//s"]) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: STATE is an absolute path of plain names
